title: Product Tampering and Crisis Governance
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。出版社の解答ページは未提供です。

passages.text:
In autumn 1982, seven people in the Chicago area died after taking capsules from packages into which cyanide had been maliciously introduced. The deaths created an urgent public-health problem, but the first analytical task was classification. Investigators had to distinguish contamination during manufacture from tampering after products had entered distribution. That distinction affected which packages might be dangerous, what evidence had to be preserved, and which institutions should act.

The manufacturer warned the public and recalled products while the scope and source of the danger were still uncertain. This response is often summarized as proof that a costly recall automatically restores trust. The evidence supports a narrower claim: rapid warning and broad removal can reduce exposure and signal that consumer safety has priority. Whether the same action restores reputation depends on prior trust, message credibility, later evidence, competitors, and what would have happened under another response.

The episode also changed the environment in which firms made decisions. The US Food and Drug Administration issued tamper-resistant packaging requirements for most nonprescription drugs in 1982, and federal legislation in 1983 made tampering with packaged consumer products a crime. Packaging could now provide visible evidence of interference. Yet “tamper-resistant” does not mean “tamper-proof.” A seal can raise the cost of interference and alert a consumer after it is broken; it cannot eliminate every malicious act.

The durable lesson is therefore institutional rather than heroic. A company needs traceable distribution, a threshold for precautionary action, coordination with public authorities, and a way to revise claims as evidence changes. Regulators need rules that protect consumers without pretending that design alone removes crime. The public needs warnings that state what is known, what remains uncertain, and what action is justified now. Good crisis governance does not erase uncertainty; it makes uncertainty governable.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: A costly recall always restores a company's reputation.

options.label: B
options.text: Tamper-resistant packaging can eliminate every malicious act.

options.label: C
options.text: Effective crisis governance separates causal classification, immediate protection, institutional change, and later evaluation.

options.label: D
options.text: Public warnings should wait until all uncertainty has disappeared.

questions.answer: 正解：C。本文は原因の分類、曝露を減らす即時対応、規制・制度の変化、信頼回復の慎重な事後評価を区別します。A・B・Dはいずれも本文が明確に限定する主張です。

questions.prompt: Why was it important to distinguish manufacturing contamination from post-distribution tampering?

options.label: A
options.text: The distinction changed the likely danger range, relevant evidence, and responsible institutions.

options.label: B
options.text: Both causes always implicate exactly the same lots, stores, and records.

options.label: C
options.text: The distinction mattered only for advertising after the crisis.

options.label: D
options.text: Post-distribution tampering requires no preservation of criminal evidence.

questions.answer: 正解：A。製造時なら工程・ロット記録が中心となり、流通後なら店舗・地域・包装・犯罪証拠が重要になるため、危険範囲と担当機関も変わります。B～Dはこの分類の実務的効果を否定します。

questions.prompt: The word “scope” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: the geographic and product range of the possible danger

options.label: B
options.text: the manufacturer's previous advertising budget

options.label: C
options.text: the chemical formula of every capsule

options.label: D
options.text: the legal penalty imposed in 1983

questions.answer: 正解：A。ここでscopeは、危険がどの地域・製品・包装に及ぶ可能性があるかという範囲です。B～Dは評判、化学組成、刑罰であり文脈上の意味ではありません。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage reject the claim that a broad recall automatically restores trust?

options.label: A
options.text: Reputation also depends on prior trust, message credibility, later evidence, competitors, and an unobserved alternative response.

options.label: B
options.text: A recall can never reduce consumer exposure.

options.label: C
options.text: Trust is determined only by packaging design.

options.label: D
options.text: The public had complete information before the recall.

questions.answer: 正解：A。回収は曝露低減と安全優先の合図にはなりますが、評判という結果には複数要因と観察できない反実仮想が関わります。B～Dは本文の限定的な因果主張と矛盾します。

questions.prompt: How did the 1982 packaging requirements and the 1983 federal legislation differ?

options.label: A
options.text: The requirements introduced visible barriers or evidence of interference, while the legislation made packaged-product tampering a federal crime.

options.label: B
options.text: Both measures merely asked firms to advertise more often.

options.label: C
options.text: The packaging rules criminalized consumers, while the law removed all seals.

options.label: D
options.text: The legislation came first and applied only to prescription drugs.

questions.answer: 正解：A。1982年の規則は多くの一般用医薬品に改ざん抵抗性包装を求め、1983年の法律は包装消費財の改ざんを犯罪化しました。B～Dは機能、順序、対象を誤ります。

questions.prompt: What does “tamper-resistant” mean according to the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: It guarantees that malicious interference is physically impossible.

options.label: B
options.text: It can deter interference or reveal it after a seal is broken, but it cannot remove all risk.

options.label: C
options.text: It applies only after every criminal has been identified.

options.label: D
options.text: It makes warnings and investigations unnecessary.

questions.answer: 正解：B。sealは改ざんのコストを上げ、破損を消費者に知らせますが、あらゆる悪意ある行為を不可能にはしません。A・C・Dはresistantをproofと取り違えます。

questions.prompt: Why should a public warning separate what is known, what is uncertain, and what action is justified now?

options.label: A
options.text: It preserves credibility while explaining precaution before the investigation is complete.

options.label: B
options.text: It allows officials to present every hypothesis as confirmed fact.

options.label: C
options.text: It ensures that no later revision will ever be necessary.

options.label: D
options.text: It hides uncertainty until public concern disappears.

questions.answer: 正解：A。確定事項・不確実性・現在取るべき行動を分ければ、調査途中でも予防措置の根拠を示し、断定しすぎず信頼性を保てます。B～Dは透明性と更新可能性を損ないます。

questions.prompt: What does it mean to make uncertainty governable?

options.label: A
options.text: Define decision thresholds and responsibilities, collect evidence over time, and revise actions and claims as findings change.

options.label: B
options.text: Pretend that packaging design has already eliminated crime.

options.label: C
options.text: Delay all action until investigators know every detail.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep no record of how warnings and recall boundaries changed.

questions.answer: 正解：A。不確実性を消すのでなく、行動閾値、責任、検査、更新時点、訂正履歴を設け、証拠に応じて主張と対応を変えられる状態にします。B～Dは不確実性の管理を妨げます。

questions.prompt: Which information package would best support a public warning during the first 24 hours?

options.label: A
options.text: Affected products and locations, the suspected hazard, confirmed facts versus hypotheses, consumer actions, responsible agencies, and the next update time

options.label: B
options.text: Only a promise that the company will certainly recover its reputation

options.label: C
options.text: A statement that every package is safe because a seal exists

options.label: D
options.text: Unlabeled rumors with no instructions or update plan

questions.answer: 正解：A。対象製品・地域、危険、確認済み事項と仮説、消費者行動、担当機関、次回更新を示すと、回収範囲を広げる・狭める証拠も追跡できます。B～Dは行動可能性と検証可能性を欠きます。
